Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Our opening proposal reflects the strength of the claims, the $64 million in disputed charges, and the value of reaching every identified member without a claims barrier. We are prepared to discuss the amounts, but automatic distribution and protection of any fee amount the court does not award are important terms.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline is prepared to resolve the litigation with automatic payments to the identified class, but your opening proposal exceeds our total authorized settlement outlay. Our offer preserves automatic distribution and gives the class the benefit of any fee amount the court declines to award.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s commitment to automatic payments and to ensuring any unawarded fee benefits the class. To put more of the settlement value directly in members’ hands while keeping the overall outlay at the level of your offer, we propose the following revised allocation.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: Because Brightline’s records identify the affected members, a claims process would needlessly reduce recovery. We propose a substantial, automatically distributed class fund, with any fee amount the court does not award returned to the class rather than Brightline. This is an opening proposal, subject to negotiation and court approval.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: defense
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: Brightline agrees that identified members should not face a claims barrier. We cannot meet the opening amounts, but offer a substantial automatically distributed fund and will not seek to retain any fee amount the court declines to award.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s commitment to automatic distribution and to returning any court-unawarded fee amount to the class. Given the scale of the charged renewals and the value of resolving the claims for all identified members, we propose the following revised terms.

private_notes.private_reasoning: The class has a substantial merits case but faces certification risk and delay. An automatic distribution is especially valuable because Brightline can identify all members. Open above a reasonable settlement range while preserving strong distribution and fee protections. The firm's compensation is fixed, so fees should be justified by class benefit rather than firm economics.

The class has strong merits but faces meaningful certification and trial risk. Automatic distribution is important because Brightline can identify every member. Open with a substantial fund and reasonable fees, while preserving the class’s benefit if the court reduces the fee request.

Neither opening proposal is within Brightline’s $40 million all-in authority. Make credible but firm offers below the cap, preserving automatic distribution and addressing each firm’s stated priorities. Do not accept either opening term sheet.

The defense’s offer provides a substantial, immediate class recovery through automatic payments, but a counter can seek to shift more of the same apparent total outlay to class members. The firm has no compensation incentive tied to the fee, so prioritize the class fund. Preserve automatic distribution and the term that any unawarded fee reverts to the class.

The defense offer provides certain, automatic recovery, but the $28 million fund is below the class’s expected trial recovery before accounting for delay and certification risk. Counter at a meaningful midpoint while preserving automatic distribution and ensuring court-rejected fee amounts benefit the class. The firm has no financial incentive to maximize fees.

Hargrove Lane’s latest term sheet provides automatic distribution, directs any unawarded fees to the class, and has a total outlay of $32 million, within Brightline’s $40 million authorization. Accepting it resolves the overlapping litigation; Whitcombe Reyes’s latest proposal exceeds the authorized cap.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The parties reached the settlement through confidential, arm’s-length negotiations. Class counsel evaluated the proposed relief in light of the claims, litigation risks, and the practical benefits of automatic payment to identified class members. The parties agreed to a $30,000,000 class fund, automatic distribution, and a separate fee request subject to court approval. Consistent with the confidentiality of the negotiations, this statement does not disclose negotiation communications or offers.
